name: Maurya Empire
summary: A major empire founded by Chandragupta Maurya; reached a large extent under Ashoka.
notes: Territorial extent varied by reign. The sample outline is schematic.

name: Gupta Empire
summary: A major North Indian imperial power associated with rulers such as Samudragupta and Chandragupta II.
notes: Political control and tributary influence were not identical; outline is schematic.

name: Kushan Empire
summary: An empire spanning parts of Central Asia and northern South Asia; Kanishka is a prominent ruler.
notes: The map shows only a simplified South Asian footprint.

name: Satavahana Dynasty
summary: A long-lasting Deccan dynasty with shifting centres and influence.
notes: Dates and territorial limits are debated; outline is schematic.

name: Pallava Kingdom
summary: A major power in northern Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas, known for its temple architecture.
notes: The sample polygon represents a broad core region, not a surveyed border.

name: Chola Empire
summary: A powerful Tamil dynasty whose influence expanded across southern India and overseas under some rulers.
notes: Overseas expeditions and tributary influence are not represented as continuous land borders.

name: Pala Empire
summary: A Buddhist imperial dynasty that ruled much of Bengal and Bihar at its height.
notes: Territorial extent changed considerably over time; outline is schematic.

name: Rashtrakuta Empire
summary: A major Deccan empire that competed with the Palas and Gurjara-Pratiharas.
notes: Sample outline approximates a broad core region.

name: Delhi Sultanate
summary: A succession of dynasties ruling from Delhi, with changing reach across the subcontinent.
notes: This broad outline is not valid for every year; use the year slider as a period filter only.

name: Vijayanagara Empire
summary: A major South Indian empire founded in the 14th century; its power changed after the Battle of Talikota.
notes: The sample outline is schematic and does not depict all tributary relationships.

name: Bahmani Sultanate
summary: A Deccan sultanate that later fragmented into successor sultanates.
notes: Its boundaries fluctuated; the displayed polygon is indicative only.

name: Mughal Empire
summary: A major early-modern empire founded by Babur, reaching a large extent under Aurangzeb.
notes: This outline represents an approximate high-water extent, not the territory in every year.

name: Maratha Confederacy
summary: A confederacy whose influence expanded widely in the 18th century.
notes: Confederate influence, chauth claims and directly administered territory differed; outline is schematic.

name: Kingdom of Mysore
summary: A South Indian kingdom that became a major power under Haider Ali and Tipu Sultan.
notes: The sample outline approximates a late-18th-century footprint.

name: Sikh Empire
summary: An empire consolidated by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the Punjab region.
notes: Includes areas now in India and Pakistan; outline is schematic.

name: Ahom Kingdom
summary: A long-lasting kingdom in Assam, known for resisting Mughal expansion.
notes: The polygon indicates an approximate Assam core, not all historical claims.

name: Bengal Sultanate
summary: An independent sultanate that ruled Bengal for over two centuries.
notes: The historical region crossed modern India-Bangladesh borders.

name: Kingdom of Travancore
summary: A prominent princely state in the southwest of the Indian subcontinent.
notes: The sample outline is a simplified late-period footprint.
